The perimeter is the length of the closed curve, $L = \int_0^{2\pi} |f'(\theta)|\,d\theta$.

Differentiating term by term:

$$f'(\theta) = i\left(e^{i\theta} + 2e^{2i\theta} + e^{3i\theta}\right) = i\,e^{i\theta}\left(1 + e^{i\theta}\right)^2.$$

Taking the modulus, $|i| = 1$ and $|e^{i\theta}| = 1$, so

$$|f'(\theta)| = |1+e^{i\theta}|^2 = (1+e^{i\theta})(1+e^{-i\theta}) = 2 + 2\cos\theta.$$

Integrating over one full period:

$$L = \int_0^{2\pi} (2 + 2\cos\theta)\,d\theta = 4\pi + 2\left[\sin\theta\right]_0^{2\pi} = 4\pi.$$

The curve is closed since $f(0) = f(2\pi) = 3 + \tfrac{1}{3}$, and $f'$ vanishes only at $\theta = \pi$, which does not affect the integral.

ANSWER: $4\pi$
